units.teachingGoal: Preserve Ali's complete practical, information-judgment and participation reasons to care without beginning concept instruction.
questionsAnswered: Why is this book worth reading?

sections.title: Why AI Fundamentals matters to you
sections.teachingGoal: Preserve Ali's authored Introduction and reader relationship.
relationshipsAdded: Understanding supports better use, better judgment and informed participation.
questionsAnswered: Why should I understand AI without a technical background?
sections.learnerEvidence: The reader can name the reason that matters most to her.

units.teachingGoal: Build the principal AI families through stable reader questions, keep true nesting separate from overlapping properties and use history only to qualify rather than falsely order the ideas.
questionsAnswered: What is AI?
How did the system get its working knowledge?
Which labels describe results, information forms, continued action, physical action or breadth?
How do current, disputed and hypothetical labels fit together?

sections.title: Start here: what is artificial intelligence?
sections.teachingGoal: Give a zero-prerequisite meaning for AI through an actual photo-search system.
relationshipsAdded: AI is the broad field, not one product or method.
questionsAnswered: What does AI mean in this book?
sections.learnerEvidence: The reader can identify the information, task and worked-out result in an ordinary AI interaction.

sections.title: How did it get its working knowledge?
sections.teachingGoal: Keep human-supplied expert knowledge, machine learning and deep learning together as construction approaches, while excluding trivial automation and teaching the true nesting relationship.
relationshipsAdded: Human experts can supply connected knowledge and rules; machine learning finds patterns from examples; deep learning is a type of machine learning inside AI.
questionsAnswered: Why can an expert system count as AI?
Why is one automatic threshold not a useful AI example?
What changes when a system learns from examples?
How is deep learning related to machine learning?
sections.learnerEvidence: The reader distinguishes a linked expert system from a single business rule and draws AI, machine learning and deep learning as three nested circles.

sections.title: What result does it produce?
sections.teachingGoal: Orient the reader to recognition, classification, prediction, ranking, recommendation, generation, planning and control, then explain predictive and generative as two common result families rather than the only options.
relationshipsAdded: Predictive AI estimates something about a case; generative AI creates new content; generative mechanisms may use prediction internally without making the public labels identical.
questionsAnswered: What can an AI system produce?
What makes an output predictive or generative?
Why can a generative model make predictions internally?
sections.learnerEvidence: The reader distinguishes estimating an existing email's category from producing a new email and does not treat predictive/generative as the only possible results.

sections.title: What information can it connect, what happens after an answer and does it act physically?
sections.teachingGoal: Teach information-form, continued-action and physical-world properties under three explicit reader questions without implying a historical succession.
relationshipsAdded: The three labels answer different questions and may overlap predictive or generative work; an agent can stop at a designed approval point and remain agentic.
questionsAnswered: What does multimodal add?
What makes a complete system agentic?
What makes AI embodied?
sections.learnerEvidence: The reader can apply each label to an actual product without turning them into intelligence levels.

sections.title: Specialised, general-purpose, AGI and ASI describe breadth claims
sections.teachingGoal: Move from current bounded and broad-use systems to disputed and hypothetical categories with full names before acronyms.
relationshipsAdded: General-purpose current systems are not thereby AGI; AGI is disputed and ASI is hypothetical.
questionsAnswered: What would AGI require beyond broad current usefulness?
What does ASI propose?
sections.learnerEvidence: The reader explains AGI and ASI without treating either as a current product or inevitable next step.

sections.title: A timeline that is not a ladder, one product synthesis and learner checks
sections.teachingGoal: Use bounded history to prevent a false succession, separate true nesting from overlapping properties, test transfer with exact correction routes and hand off to Chapter 2.
relationshipsAdded: AI contains machine learning contains deep learning; other labels answer different questions and can overlap.
questionsAnswered: Did these ideas replace one another?
Can I reconstruct, explain and use the relationships on an unfamiliar product?
What will Chapter 2 add?
sections.learnerEvidence: The reader completes Recognise, Explain, Draw and Use tasks with reasoned answers, follows a named correction route for each misconception and can state the next unresolved system question.
